scope: Publicly observable ESXi 8.0.3 DirectPath owner activation, reboot, dependency expansion and VM admission behavior; no private implementation inference

snapshot.result: both functions were capable, enabled and active, shared dependentDevice 0000:01:00.0, and every CLI collector completed successfully

admissionPair.result: verdict=pass; phase logs captured AH collision markers for the cross-VM and same-VM cases; temporary VMs were removed

esxcli803.observation: hardware pci pcipassthru set --apply-now requests immediate native-to-passthrough rebinding; without --apply-now the configured request is intended for host reboot

hostPciPassthruInfo.observation: passthruEnabled is configured state, passthruActive is effective state, and dependentDevice identifies a device that must be unclaimed and may be a bridge

hostPciPassthruSystem.observation: UpdatePassthruConfig exposes the host owner configuration transaction through the public SOAP API

deviceBackingInfo.observation: static passthrough backing carries id, vendorId, deviceId, systemId and deviceName

kb309986.observation: green represents enabled and active; orange represents configured state changed but not yet active

kb434815.observation: a storage HBA with active paths can make native-driver detach return Busy; this is a consumer-specific example and is not generalized to every busy device

dedicatedDeferredBeforeReboot.result: command succeeded; Configured Owner became VM Passthru while Current Owner and native module remained unchanged

dedicatedAfterRealHostReboot.result: host uptime reset and the same BDF became Current Owner=VM Passthru with module pciPassthru

persistentVswitchBusyApplyNow.result: exit=1 with explicit vSwitch uplink error; configured and current owner remained native

persistentVswitchBusyDeferred.result: deferred request also returned exit=1 and did not persist desired passthrough state

sameBdfAfterConsumerRemoval.result: after removing the vSwitch consumer, apply-now succeeded on the same device

differentDependencySibling.result: an idle function with a different dependentDevice activated while its busy sibling remained native

sharedBridgeDependencyExpansion.result: requesting only the idle function succeeded and automatically activated both functions sharing the bridge dependency

soapExplicitRequestPreflight.result: explicit request sets containing the busy function failed with vim.hostd.pcipassthru.vswitchUplink.failed; requesting only the idle function succeeded and expanded

sharedDependencyAfterRealReboot.result: deferred request through the idle member configured both; real reboot claimed both and left the persisted vSwitch without an uplink

exclusiveAdmissionLease.result: VM-A using the first function powered on; VM-B using the second failed AH selection while A was running

leaseReleaseAndSameVmCollision.result: VM-B powered on after A released the lease; one VM containing both functions failed on its second passthrough device

observedModel.requestSet: the BDFs explicitly named by the ESXCLI or SOAP request
observedModel.ownerActivationGroup: the devices whose effective host owner changes together
observedModel.exclusiveAttachGroup: the resource boundary exclusively leased during VM admission
observedModel.resetContract: an independent recovery contract; it does not by itself determine owner grouping, admission grouping or reboot
observedModel.liveApply: possible when the resulting activation group can be claimed immediately
observedModel.rebootRequired: valid only for an explicit deferred transaction with an exact early-boot owner claim
observedModel.persistentVswitchUse: locally observed as an atomic denial for both apply-now and direct deferred requests
observedModel.requestTargetAsymmetry: on the shared bridge topology, requesting the idle member expanded to the group, while explicitly requesting the busy member or full group failed
observedModel.vmAdmission: members sharing the observed dependency formed an exclusive lease; no same-VM coalescing was observed

invariants: resolve exact identity and expand every owner activation group before consumer preflight
deny incomplete groups, unknown ownership, host-critical members and persistent host use
do not infer reboot requirement from FLR, class code, BAR size or generic busy state
return REBOOT_REQUIRED only for an explicit maintenance transaction with a proven exact boot claim
verify effective owner and provider for every expanded member after transition or reboot
lease every exclusive attach group atomically at VM admission
deny duplicate exclusive attach groups even within one VM unless an exact qualified policy proves safety
never silently remove network, storage or management consumers through sibling expansion
runtime guest PCI hotplug remains permanently disabled

remainingSoftwareWork: build versioned owner, attach, reset and physical-isolation groups from authoritative host facts
implement the durable owner executor, rollback, quarantine and observed-state commit
implement signed exact early-boot claims and post-reboot reconciliation
implement atomic multi-key attach leases with epoch and fencing
integrate Static and Dynamic assignment transactions with the MMIO/firmware planner
enforce lifecycle and runtime-hotplug negative gates through API, scheduler, launcher and QMP
provide a linearizable multi-host lease store and real power fencing for HA
limitations: The owner, reboot, dependency and VM admission behaviors were executed on ESXi 8.0.3, but the nested endpoints were QEMU virtual devices.
Physical HBA storage paths, GPU multifunction coupling, vendor reset side effects, DPC/AER recovery and boot-critical host devices still require physical-hardware qualification.
SR-IOV, ATS/PASID/PRI, peer-to-peer DMA and platform RMRR/IVMD behavior cannot be proven by the simplified nested endpoints.
The local observations justify fail-closed control-plane semantics but do not replace a per-model HCL and errata database.
